title: WoW Sold Out So Fast Blizzard Stopped Shipping It
hook: WoW sold 240,000 copies in its first 24 hours in November 2004 and all 40 launch servers filled up the same day. Blizzard held back new copies from stores until the servers could cope. Were you stuck in a two hour queue that week?
script: Did you know World of Warcraft sold out so fast that Blizzard had to stop shipping it to stores? The game launched in North America on Tuesday, November 23, 2004, the Tuesday before Thanksgiving. In the first 24 hours it sold more than 240,000 copies. That made it the fastest selling PC game ever at the time. More than 200,000 accounts were created on day one. By five in the afternoon Pacific time, over 100,000 people were playing at once. Blizzard had set up 40 servers for launch. All 40 filled up almost immediately. By the end of Thanksgiving weekend the company had added another 40 plus servers, and sales passed 350,000 copies. Players still waited in login queues of up to two hours. Demand was so far beyond the plan that Blizzard held back new shipments to retailers until it could prove the servers were stable. By the end of the holiday season the game had passed 600,000 copies in North America, Australia and New Zealand. Blizzard president Mike Morhaime called the public response simply amazing. Within a few years it would reach 12 million subscribers. Were you there for launch week, stuck in a queue? Follow for more gaming history.
